# BTicino C300X Native Agent Integration v0.3.3

First feature release after `v0.2.0`, focused on agent lifecycle management,
native MQTT migration, diagnostics, and lower write/load impact on the C300X.

## Highlights

- Home Assistant Repairs can update the native C300X agent through the
  maintenance API when the installed agent supports self-update.
- First install and fallback repair flows can install the packaged agent over
  SSH without storing SSH credentials.
- Native MQTT bridge support mirrors the legacy C300X topics and keeps broker
  settings in the agent configuration.
- Legacy `TcpDump2Mqtt` can be disabled through guarded maintenance controls
  without rewriting unrelated media startup files.
- Agent diagnostics expose safe runtime health details such as write counters,
  wake reason, open file descriptors, video state, and media startup reference
  state.
- Device-agent bundles are hash-checked so unchanged payloads, scripts, GUI
  files and firewall patches are skipped instead of rewritten.
- The doorbell camera remains on the app-like on-demand media path and is
  independent from the legacy MQTT runtime.

## Security and Privacy

- Maintenance actions are token-protected and explicit.
- SSH credentials are used only for bootstrap/fallback installation and are not
  stored.
- Diagnostics avoid token values, broker passwords, private callback URLs and
  user-specific device details.
- The repository does not ship firmware images, APKs, copied stock QML pages,
  third-party controller code or foreign MQTT runtime code.

## Notes

- The C300X must already be rooted or SSH-enabled before the native agent can be
  installed.
- The release asset must be the generated `ha-bticino-c300x.zip`; HACS uses that
  zip so the Home Assistant integration and ARMHF native-agent bundle stay
  version-aligned.
